sources.title: NGSS MS-LS1-2: Develop and use a model to describe the function of a cell as a whole and ways the parts of cells contribute to the function

steps.title: Cell membrane
steps.instruction: Trace the cell membrane all the way round.

note.text: A thin, flexible layer around the cell. It controls what goes in and out. Animal cells have no cell wall.
The nucleus holds the cell's DNA: the instructions for building and running the cell.

steps.title: Nucleolus
steps.instruction: Draw the nucleolus inside the nucleus.

note.text: A dense spot in the nucleus that makes the parts of ribosomes.
Mitochondria use oxygen and food to make ATP, the cell's energy-carrying molecule. This is cellular respiration.

steps.title: Folds
steps.instruction: Draw the folded inner membrane in each one.

note.text: The inner membrane is folded, giving it lots of surface where ATP is made.
Lysosomes are the cell's garbage disposal. Their enzymes break down food molecules and worn-out parts.

steps.title: Centrioles
steps.instruction: Trace the pair of centrioles, at right angles.

note.text: Animal cells have a pair of centrioles near the nucleus. They help organize the cell when it divides.

steps.title: Ribosomes
steps.instruction: Dab a dot for each ribosome.

note.text: Ribosomes are tiny machines that build proteins. Every cell has them, even bacteria.

steps.title: Cytoplasm
steps.name: cytoplasm
steps.instruction: Tap the cytoplasm: the jelly-like fluid inside the membrane, around the organelles.

mistakes.nucleus: That's the nucleus. The cytoplasm surrounds it but doesn't go inside.
mistakes.mito: That's a mitochondrion. It sits in the cytoplasm; tap the space around it.
mistakes.lyso: That's a lysosome. Tap the fluid around it.
mistakes.centrioles: Those are centrioles. Tap the open space around them.

note.text: A jelly-like fluid filling the cell around the organelles. Many of the cell's chemical reactions happen here.

steps.title: Label the cell
steps.instruction: Pick the right name for each numbered part.

mistakes.Cell wall: Animal cells have no cell wall. This flexible outer layer is the membrane.

targets.role: Makes ATP from food and oxygen.

mistakes.Chloroplast: Animal cells have no chloroplasts. This organelle releases energy from food: a mitochondrion.

steps.title: Form fits function
steps.question: Muscle cells are packed with far more mitochondria than most cells. Why?

options.text: Muscles need lots of energy, and mitochondria make the ATP that supplies it
options.feedback: Yes. Moving your body takes a lot of energy, so muscle cells have many mitochondria making ATP.
The nucleus holds the DNA. Mitochondria make ATP for energy.
They supply energy. Busy muscle cells need a lot of it.
That's the lysosomes' job. Mitochondria make ATP.

steps.title: The cell as a system
steps.question: A drug stops a cell's ribosomes working. What will the cell no longer be able to do?

options.feedback: Right. Ribosomes build proteins, which the cell needs for almost everything. The parts depend on each other.
The nucleus stores DNA. Ribosomes build proteins.
Lysosomes do that, though their enzymes are proteins made by ribosomes.
The membrane does that. Ribosomes build proteins.
